leaves.name: heckeJ1DS
leaves.doc: aftate-fix2 (r16-det fold): the Hecke operators on J_1(N) over Q. For N >= 2, every model X of Diamond-Shurman's X_1(N)_alg with chosen generators (j_X, t_X) of K(X) = Q(j, f_1) (IsX1Gen: the integer relations of (j_X, t_X) are those of (j(tau), f_1(tau)), f_1 = T5Glue.weber <1,tau> (1/N)), every rational point P0 and every Jacobian (J, aj) (Albanese property): there are endomorphisms T_p (every prime p) and <d> (d in (Z/N)^*) of J over Q acting on degree-0 divisor classes of the points x_tau (AtTau: the complex point where every g in K(X) whose meromorphic function on H has a limit c at tau is regular with value c) by DS's double-coset formulas: T_p[x_tau] = sum_{j<p} [x_{(tau+j)/p}] + [x_{g(p tau)}] (last term for p not dividing N; g in SL_2(Z), N | c, d = p mod N), <d>[x_tau] = [x_{g tau}].

leaves.source: Diamond-Shurman, A First Course in Modular Forms, GTM 228 (2005), 6.3 (pp. 226-227), Prop. 5.2.1 (p. 171), 7.9 (p. 300); Shimura 1971 7.2 (unread)

leaves.name: afShimura
leaves.doc: aftate-fix2 (r16-det fold): Shimura's A_f over Q. For a newform f in S_2(Gamma_1(N)) with nebentypus chi, N >= 2, X, (j_X, t_X), P0, (J, aj) as in heckeJ1DS and any T_p, <d> with DS's divisor action: K_f is a number field, and there are A, pi : J -> A and theta : K_f -> End^0(A) with IsAfQuotient (pi surjective, kills I_f J, universal among homomorphisms to abelian varieties killing I_f J; I_f = image of the kernel of T_p -> a_p(f), <d> -> chi(d) on the free algebra) and IsAfAction (theta(a_p) is the endomorphism induced by T_p, theta(chi(d)) the one induced by <d>).
leaves.flag: pending review (inbox 10a: new printed leaf, GLUE until a reviewer rates it); unread: new printed leaf (Shimura 1973 Thm 1: the Q-rational quotient A_f = J/I_f J with the coefficient-field action; read by the locator audit, row R16, pp. 526-527; DS Def. 6.6.3, Prop. 6.6.4 over C)
leaves.source: Shimura, On the factors of the jacobian variety of a modular function field, J. Math. Soc. Japan 25 (1973), Thm 1, pp. 526-527 (read by the locator audit, row R16); Diamond-Shurman GTM 228 (2005), Def. 6.6.3 (p. 241), Prop. 6.6.4 (p. 242) (AI-read by r16-close)

leaves.name: afCharpolyDS965
leaves.doc: r16-det: Diamond-Shurman Thm 9.6.5 at k = 2 for the Section 9.5 realization on A_f, over K_{f,lambda}, universal over A_f. For every (A, pi, theta) that is DS's A_f (afShimura's characterization, for any X, generators, P0, Jacobian and Hecke operators as in heckeJ1DS), every prime l and every place lambda | l of K_f: for p not dividing N l every arithmetic Frobenius sigma at p acting on V_lambda = K_lambda (x)_{Q_l (x) K_f} V_l(A) (rho_{f,lambda}, DS Exercise 9.5.2(a)) has characteristic polynomial X^2 - a_p X + chi(p) p over K_lambda. Statement = aftate-fix2's AfTateLam.AfTateDSLambda verbatim (AfTateLam.afCharpolyDS965_iff, Iff.rfl); it implies r16-close's glue AfDetLambda (AfTateLam.afDetLambda_of_ds965).

leaves.name: igusaGL2DS
leaves.doc: x1-igusa: Igusa's theorem in its printed form, Gal(Q(j, E_j[N])/Q(j)) = GL_2(Z/N) for Diamond-Shurman's E_j : y^2 = 4x^3 - g x - g, g = 27j/(j-1728), j transcendental. For N >= 1, every basis e : (Z/N)^2 = E_j[N] over an algebraic closure of Q(j) and every g in GL_2(Z/N), some sigma in Aut(Q(j)bar/Q(j)) acts on E_j[N] as g in the basis e. Used through X1Igusa.x1PointsConjugate_of_igusaGL2DS (the dictionary IsX1Model -> IsX1AlgDS, aftate-or).

leaves.name: y3FineModuliAbP
leaves.doc: y3-fix, printed form (representability, one object: the fine moduli scheme Y3 with its universal family): the moduli problem of abelian surfaces with an action of the maximal order O of B = (2,-3|Q) and full level-3 structure in Mumford's form (GIT Def. 7.1, O-linear: at every geometric point s the sections eta(a), a in O/3O, are exactly the points of A_s(k)[3]) is represented over Q by a proper smooth curve (some (Y, Phi) satisfies R1fpPropsAbP; no Qbar-point clause). Buzzard, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) section 1; Boutot-Carayol, Asterisque 196-197 (1991) ch. III; Milne 1979; Mumford GIT Def. 7.1, Thm 7.9; locators UNVERIFIED. Consequence form: universal property used on proper smooth curve bases and read on field points; base Q. Equivalent to the kernel's level form over Q-schemes (Y3Fix.toKer, Y3Fix.ofKer from mumfordTorsionAlgClosed).
leaves.flag: pending review (inbox 10b: new printed leaf, GLUE until a reviewer rates it); locator UNVERIFIED; reading risk: the kernel's moduli problem has no polarization (Lemma P: the type-mu principal polarization exists and is unique); Milne 1979 and Boutot-Carayol include the polarization
leaves.source: Buzzard, Integral models of certain Shimura curves, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) section 1 (representability of the QM moduli problem with level structure, projective smooth curve over Z[1/ND]); Boutot-Carayol, Asterisque 196-197 (1991) ch. III; Milne, Points on Shimura varieties mod p (1979); Mumford GIT Def. 7.1 (level-n structure on geometric fibres) and Thm 7.9; base Q, full level 3; locators UNVERIFIED

leaves.name: deligneCanonicalModelY3EveryH
leaves.doc: y3-fix, printed form (one object: Y3 = Sh_K3(B^x, H^+-) with its moduli interpretation and canonical-model property): for every witness (Y, Phi) of R1fpPropsAbP there is Psi : H x (B tensor A_f)^x -> Y(C), onto with fibres the B^x_+ \ . / K3 classes, holomorphic in tau, with the moduli interpretation at g in O-hat^x in the print's H_1 / Hodge form (IsHodgeH1: for an analytic uniformization A(C) = Lie A / H_1(A,Z), an O-linear beta : B_R = H_1(A,R) with beta(O) = H_1(A,Z) and beta(M J_tau) = i beta(M), J_tau = h_tau(i)) and Shimura's reciprocity law at CM points (conventions existential). Deligne, Sem. Bourbaki 389 (1971) section 4 (moduli interpretation by (H_1(A,Q), h_A) = (B, h)) and section 5 (Cor. 5.7 / Ex. 5.8 per locators.md R1); Milne, Introduction to Shimura varieties sections 8 and 14; locators UNVERIFIED. The passage to the kernel's lattice form is proved (Y3Fix.lattice_of_hodge).

leaves.name: sga7_IX_Cor3_3
leaves.doc: sga33-steps, printed form (specialized to traits): SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, Cor. 3.3, p. 348 (semistable reduction: Def. 3.4, p. 349; locator from the 11-16 reading in the task brief): for an extension of DVRs O in O' (O' meet K = O, any K'/K, no henselian condition), Neron models N, N' with N semistable, the canonical u : N x_O O' -> N' (generic fibre the identification, bcDVR) induces an isomorphism N0 x_O O' = N'0 (an iso of open subschemes over N').
